t: Varanasi was the centre of the Kingdom of Kashi in the time of the Buddha, who first taught at nearby Sarnath, and it became a city of Hindu pilgrimage whose ghats on the Ganges are used for bathing and cremation.

It was raided and ravaged in 1033 and 1194, sacked around 1567, and had temples destroyed on the order of Aurangzeb, and much of the present city was built in the 18th century under Maratha and Bhumihar patronage.

A line of rulers took the title Maharaja of Benares from 1740, the East India Company acquired the city in 1775, and its Sanskrit college of 1791 and Banaras Hindu University of 1916 continued its record as a centre of learning.
dyk: In the 1830s James Prinsep's census put the number of temples in the city at around 1000, according to the account Rev. M. A. Sherring published in 1868.

f.founded: In Hindu scriptures the city, under its name Kashi, was founded by Shiva. Excavations in 2014 found artefacts dating back to 800 BCE, and two sites near the city, Aktha and Ramnagar, yielded artefacts dating back to 1800 BCE.
f.where: On the left, crescent-shaped bank of the Ganges in the south-eastern part of Uttar Pradesh, India, between the river's confluences with the Varuna and the Assi stream, 121 km downstream of Prayagraj.
f.known: Hindu pilgrimage, death and mourning; the ghats on the Ganges; the Kashi Vishwanath Temple; Sarnath, where the Buddha first taught; the Bhakti poets Kabir, Ravidas and Tulsidas; Sanskrit learning and Banaras Hindu University; silk weaving
f.today: Varanasi is a city and the headquarters of a district in Uttar Pradesh, India, and remains a place of pilgrimage for Hindus, Buddhists and Jains.
